frozen_original.title: Agricultural Sector Devastated: China Soybean Exports Collapse 72%, $14.9B Loss
frozen_original.synopsis: China's retaliatory tariffs in 2025 reduced U.S. agricultural exports to China from $24.5 billion in 2024 to just $8.4 billion in 2025, a two-thirds decline and the lowest annual figure in over two decades, per NDSU Agricultural Trade Monitor analysis. NDSU estimated the annualized China-specific agricultural export shortfall at $14.9 billion — 41% larger than the $10.6 billion shortfall during the 2018–2019 trade war. Soybeans accounted for $6.8 billion of the loss; beef and cotton each contributed $1.3 billion; corn $333 million; and tree nuts $964 million. For the first time in more than 20 years, Chinese importers purchased no soybeans from the U.S. autumn 2025 harvest, forcing American farmers to store their crops as prices fell to a five-year low. Brazil's soybean exports to China hit record levels in 2025, topping 85 million metric tons — an 18% increase — as U.S. market share evaporated.

frozen_original.title: Trump Uses Unsecured iPhone Despite Repeated Security Warnings
frozen_original.synopsis: Throughout his first term, Trump refused to use a government-issued secure phone, instead relying on personal iPhones that intelligence officials warned were vulnerable to interception by Chinese and Russian intelligence services. The New York Times reported in 2018 that Chinese intelligence had been listening to Trump's calls and using the information gathered to influence his thinking and identify his advisors' vulnerabilities. Despite multiple briefings from the NSA and Secret Service about the risks, Trump continued using the unsecured devices. The practice violated established protocol for protecting presidential communications and created significant counterintelligence exposure. Officials were reluctant to brief Trump on certain sensitive matters knowing his phone habits.
